- Located in Rajkot, Gujarat - a hub for engineering industries, with OEM-approved raw material suppliers and heat treatment service providers stationed locally, giving faster and lower-cost service
- Rajkot's skilled labour availability and labour-friendly environment supports reliability of supply
- Over 20 years of operating history as one of the leading quality-assured gear, gear box and transmission component manufacturers in Rajkot
- Majority of parts self-certified by OEM customers and used directly at their assembly line - an embedded, quality-approved supplier position

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Export concentration collapse / geopolitical exposure — The Company recorded Nil export sales in FY2025-26, which management attributes to external factors and war tensions among other countries; the entire top line is now dependent on the domestic market, and MD&A separately lists 'Tense situations amongst the Country' as a risk factor.
- Raw material price volatility — MD&A Threats, Risk and Concern explicitly lists 'Prices of Raw materials' as a risk; as a machined-gear manufacturer buying OEM-approved steel and outsourcing heat treatment, input cost swings bear directly on margin.
- Changes in government policies and regulations — Explicitly flagged in MD&A Threats, Risk and Concern; the Company also credits government policy with strengthening its industry structure, so the same lever cuts both ways.
- Cyclicality and volatility of the automobile industry — MD&A lists 'Volatile in Automobile Industry' as a risk factor; the Company operates in a single manufacturing segment supplying automotive transmission components, so it has no segment diversification to absorb an auto downturn.
- Competition — Explicitly flagged in MD&A Threats, Risk and Concern; the auto component sector spans large corporations to micro enterprises across manufacturing clusters nationwide, with an organised segment competing to supply high-value precision parts to OEMs.
- Manpower availability and dependence on skilled labour — MD&A lists 'Manpower' as a risk factor; the Company's stated moat rests on Rajkot's skilled labour availability, and its total employee count is under ten (below the threshold requiring a POSH committee), making it acutely dependent on a very small workforce.
- Foreign exchange rate fluctuation — Explicitly flagged in MD&A Threats, Risk and Concern, and relevant to the Company's stated intent to seek clients abroad and pursue foreign technical collaborations.
- Single-segment and single-location concentration — The Company operates in one manufacturing segment (gears, gear boxes and transmission components) from Rajkot, Gujarat, so segment reporting is not applicable; any disruption at that site or in that product line has no offsetting business.
- Promoter/related-party funding dependence — The Directors' Report discloses an unsecured loan availed from a Director, treated as exempted deposit, with an outstanding balance as at 31 March 2026; the Company's funding is therefore reliant on promoter support rather than external debt securities, which it does not have.

Parts are made and tested to German DIN specification and the majority are self-certified by OEM customers and used directly on their assembly lines. It operates as a single manufacturing segment serving automotive, agricultural and engineering applications; in FY2025-26 there were no export sales and all revenue was domestic.

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no named capex or capacity-expansion project. The only forward manufacturing intent stated is in the MD&A 'Future Plan of Company', where the Company says it is on the threshold of manufacturing assembly of gear boxes for automobiles and machine tools, and that it welcomes foreign collaborations in technical knowhow with buyback arrangements for manufacture of gear boxes, geared motors, ground gears and similar components; no site, cost or timeline is attached to either. outlook.body:
- Turnover increased year on year despite nil export sales in FY2025-26, which management attributes to war tensions among other countries; management is hopeful of continuing this profitable position and strives for better performance in the next period
- Rajkot location advantage - an engineering hub with OEM-approved raw material suppliers and heat treatment service providers nearby, plus skilled labour availability, enabling faster and more cost-competitive service to customers
- Auto component industry growth potential from a rising population and increasing vehicle demand across segments, with post-Covid preference for personal vehicles over public transport supporting demand
- Government initiatives for the auto industry, including the ATMANIRBHAR and MAKE IN INDIA themes, seen as a path of opportunity for the Company
- Indian macro backdrop described as resilient - FY2025-26 real GDP growth of 7.6% and real GVA growth of 7.7% - supporting broad-based sectoral expansion
- Auto component industry accounted for 2.3% of India's GDP in FY25 with sector GDP contribution expected to reach 5-7% by 2026
- Two-wheeler segment dominates domestic auto volumes and commercial vehicle demand is strengthening on logistics and passenger transport expansion; electrification of three-wheelers and small passenger cars is an emerging trend shaping market growth
- Global growth headwind - projected at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027, slower than the recent pace of about 3.4% in 2024-25, with the Middle East war from February 2026 clouding the forecast
- Management notes it is very difficult to predict the future situation but is optimistic towards growth of the business
